name: Saul
note: The length of his reign is lost from the Hebrew text of 1 Samuel 13:1; Acts 13:21 gives forty years.

name: Ish-bosheth
office: King of Israel at Mahanaim, rival to David
note: Reigned two years over the northern tribes while David reigned in Hebron (2 Samuel 2:10).

name: David
office: King of Judah at Hebron, then of all Israel
note: Seven and a half years in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:4–5).

name: Solomon
note: Forty years (1 Kings 11:42); the kingdom divided at his death.

name: Ahaziah
note: Killed by Jehu together with Joram of Israel.

name: Athaliah
note: Daughter of Ahab; seized the throne on her son Ahaziah's death.

name: Uzziah (Azariah)
note: Struck with leprosy, he left the government to his son Jotham (2 Kings 15:5).

name: Hezekiah
note: Many scholars (Albright, McFall, Kitchen) also posit a coregency with Ahaz from 729 BC to reconcile 2 Kings 18:1, 9–10 with 18:13.

name: Josiah
note: Killed at Megiddo by Pharaoh Necho in 609 BC.

name: Jehoahaz (Shallum)
note: Reigned three months before Necho deposed him.

name: Jehoiachin (Jeconiah)
note: Reigned three months, then taken to Babylon (597 BC); released by Evil-merodach in 562 BC.

name: Zedekiah
note: Last king of Judah. Jerusalem fell in 587 or 586 BC: the date is debated (Albright 587, Thiele 586).

name: Zimri
note: Reigned seven days (1 Kings 16:15).

name: Tibni
note: Half the people followed Tibni and half Omri (1 Kings 16:21–22).

name: Omri
note: Founded Samaria; Assyrian texts call Israel 'the house of Omri'.

name: Ahab
note: Fought Shalmaneser III at Qarqar in 853 BC (Kurkh monolith).

name: Jehu
note: Shown paying tribute to Shalmaneser III on the Black Obelisk (841 BC).

name: Zechariah (Zachariah)
note: Reigned six months (2 Kings 15:8).

name: Shallum
note: Reigned one month (2 Kings 15:13).

name: Menahem
note: Paid tribute to Tiglath-Pileser III ('Pul').

name: Pekah
note: His twenty years (2 Kings 15:27) are explained by Thiele as counted from a rival reign in Gilead begun in 752 BC.

name: Hoshea
note: Last king of Israel; Samaria fell to Assyria in 722 BC.

name: Shoshenq I (Shishak)
note: Usually identified with Shishak, who plundered Jerusalem in Rehoboam's fifth year (1 Kings 14:25). Egyptian dates for this period are uncertain by a decade or more.

name: Taharqa (Tirhakah)
note: Came out against Sennacherib (2 Kings 19:9); the title 'king of Kush' may anticipate his accession.

name: Necho II
note: Killed Josiah at Megiddo (609 BC) and was defeated by Nebuchadnezzar at Carchemish (605 BC).

name: Apries (Hophra)
note: Pharaoh Hophra of Jeremiah 44:30.

name: Shalmaneser III
note: Not named in the Bible, but his inscriptions name Ahab (Qarqar, 853 BC) and Jehu (Black Obelisk, 841 BC).

name: Adad-nirari III
note: An inscription records tribute from Joash of Samaria.

name: Tiglath-Pileser III (Pul)
note: Called Pul in 2 Kings 15:19 and 1 Chronicles 5:26, the name he used as king of Babylon (729–727 BC).

name: Shalmaneser V
note: Besieged Samaria (2 Kings 17:3–5).

name: Sargon II
note: Claimed the capture of Samaria (722/720 BC).

name: Sennacherib
note: Invaded Judah in 701 BC (2 Kings 18–19; the Taylor prism).

name: Ashurbanipal (Osnappar)
note: Usually identified with 'the great and noble Osnappar' of Ezra 4:10. The end of his reign (631 or 627 BC) is uncertain.

name: Ashur-etil-ilani
note: Dates uncertain.

name: Sinsharishkun
note: Nineveh fell in 612 BC.

name: Ashur-uballit II
note: Last king of Assyria; Necho marched to support him in 609 BC.

name: Merodach-baladan II
note: Sent envoys to Hezekiah (Isaiah 39:1); king of Babylon twice, 722–710 and briefly in 703 BC.

name: Merodach-baladan II
note: Second reign of about nine months.

name: Nebuchadnezzar II
note: Took Jerusalem in 597 BC and destroyed it in 587/586 BC.

name: Amel-Marduk (Evil-merodach)
note: Released Jehoiachin from prison (2 Kings 25:27).

name: Neriglissar
note: Probably the Nergal-sharezer present at the fall of Jerusalem (Jeremiah 39:3).

name: Labashi-Marduk
note: Reigned a few months.

name: Nabonidus
note: Spent about ten years at Tayma in Arabia, leaving his son Belshazzar in charge of Babylon.

name: Belshazzar
note: Ruled Babylon for his father Nabonidus (Daniel 5); the start of the regency (c. 553/550 BC) is approximate.

name: Cyrus the Great
note: King of Persia from 559 BC; conquered Babylon in 539 BC and let the exiles return (Ezra 1).

name: Cambyses II
note: Conquered Egypt in 525 BC.

name: Bardiya
note: Reigned a few months in 522 BC; Darius claimed he was an impostor, the magus Gaumata.

name: Darius I (the Great)
note: The Temple was finished in his sixth year (Ezra 6:15).

name: Xerxes I (Ahasuerus)
note: The Ahasuerus of Esther and Ezra 4:6.

name: Artaxerxes I
note: Sent Ezra (458 BC, if Artaxerxes I) and Nehemiah (445 BC).

name: Xerxes II
note: Reigned 45 days.

name: Darius II
note: 'Darius the Persian' of Nehemiah 12:22 is Darius II or, less likely, Darius III.

name: Darius III
note: Defeated by Alexander; killed in 330 BC.

name: Alexander the Great
office: King of Macedon, conqueror of Persia
note: King of Macedon from 336 BC; Judaea passed to him in 332 BC.

name: Ptolemy I Soter
note: Satrap of Egypt from 323 BC, king from 305 BC.

name: Ptolemy II Philadelphus
note: By tradition (Letter of Aristeas) the Law was translated into Greek at his request.

name: Ptolemy IV Philopator
note: Defeated Antiochus III at Raphia (217 BC); the villain of 3 Maccabees.

name: Ptolemy V Epiphanes
note: Lost Judaea to Antiochus III (Panium); the Rosetta Stone is a decree of his reign.

name: Ptolemy VI Philometor
note: Ruled jointly with his brother Ptolemy VIII and Cleopatra II from 170 to 164 BC and was briefly expelled (164–163 BC).

name: Ptolemy VIII Physcon
note: Also co-ruler 170–164 BC and sole king 164–163 BC; sole king again from 145 BC, with a break in 131–126 BC.

name: Ptolemy IX Lathyros
note: First reign, with his mother Cleopatra III.

name: Ptolemy IX Lathyros
note: Second reign.

name: Ptolemy XII Auletes
note: First reign; expelled 58 BC.

name: Ptolemy XII Auletes
note: Restored by Rome, 55 BC.

name: Cleopatra VII
note: The last Ptolemaic ruler, with her brothers Ptolemy XIII and XIV and her son Caesarion as co-rulers.

name: Seleucus I Nicator
note: Satrap of Babylon from 321 BC (the Seleucid era counts from 312/311 BC); king from 305 BC.

name: Antiochus III the Great
note: Won Judaea from Egypt at Panium (200 BC).

name: Seleucus IV Philopator
note: His minister Heliodorus tried to seize the Temple treasury (2 Maccabees 3).

name: Antiochus IV Epiphanes
note: Desecrated the Temple in 167 BC.

name: Alexander Balas
note: Claimed to be a son of Antiochus IV.

name: Demetrius II Nicator
note: First reign; captured by the Parthians in 138 BC.

name: Antiochus VI Dionysus
note: A child king set up by Diodotus Tryphon against Demetrius II.

name: Demetrius II Nicator
note: Second reign after his release by the Parthians.

name: Mattathias
note: Began the revolt at Modein; died the next year (1 Maccabees 2:70).

name: Judas Maccabeus
note: Rededicated the Temple in 164 BC; killed in battle in 160 BC.

name: Jonathan Apphus
office: Leader of the Jews, high priest from 152 BC

name: Simon Thassi
note: Won independence from the Seleucids (142 BC); murdered in 135/134 BC.

name: Aristobulus I
note: The first Hasmonean to take the title of king.

name: Hyrcanus II
note: Gave up the throne to his brother after three months.

name: Aristobulus II
note: Deposed when Pompey took Jerusalem (63 BC).

name: Hyrcanus II
note: Restored by Pompey as high priest under Roman control.

name: Antigonus II Mattathias
note: Installed by the Parthians; executed after Herod took Jerusalem (37 BC).

name: Herod the Great
note: Named king by the Roman Senate in 40 BC; took Jerusalem in 37 BC. Most scholars date his death to 4 BC; a minority argue for 1 BC.

name: Herod Archelaus
office: Ethnarch of Judaea, Samaria and Idumaea
note: Deposed by Augustus in AD 6; Judaea became a Roman province (Matthew 2:22).

name: Herod Antipas
note: Beheaded John the Baptist; Jesus was sent to him by Pilate (Luke 23:7).

name: Herod Agrippa I
note: King of Philip's former tetrarchy from AD 37, Galilee from 39/40 and Judaea from 41; died at Caesarea in 44 (Acts 12:23).

name: Herod Agrippa II
note: Heard Paul with Festus (Acts 25–26). The year of his death (c. 92–100) is uncertain.

name: Augustus
note: Sole ruler after Actium (31 BC); named Augustus in 27 BC.

name: Tiberius
note: John the Baptist began preaching in his fifteenth year (Luke 3:1).

name: Claudius
note: Expelled the Jews from Rome (Acts 18:2).

name: Nero
note: The emperor to whom Paul appealed; persecuted the Christians of Rome after the fire of AD 64.

name: Titus
note: Destroyed Jerusalem and the Temple in AD 70.

name: Lucius Verus
note: Co-emperor with Marcus Aurelius.

name: Commodus
note: Co-emperor with his father from 177.

name: Caracalla
note: Co-emperor from 198.

name: Geta
note: Co-emperor from 209; murdered by Caracalla.

name: Decius
note: Ordered the first empire-wide persecution (250).

name: Valerian
note: Persecuted the church (257–260); captured by the Persians.

name: Gallienus
note: Co-emperor with his father from 253; ended the persecution.

name: Diocletian
note: Began the Great Persecution (303).

name: Maximian
note: Augustus in the West.

name: Constantius I
note: Caesar from 293; father of Constantine.

name: Galerius
note: Caesar from 293; issued an edict of toleration on his deathbed (311).

name: Maxentius
note: Defeated by Constantine at the Milvian Bridge (312).

name: Licinius
note: Joined Constantine in the Edict of Milan (313).

name: Constantine the Great
note: Proclaimed in 306; sole emperor from 324; called the Council of Nicaea (325).

name: Julian
note: Tried to restore the pagan cults.

name: Theodosius I
note: Made Nicene Christianity the religion of the empire (380); called the Council of Constantinople (381).

name: Coponius
note: First prefect after Archelaus was deposed.

name: Valerius Gratus
note: Appointed Caiaphas high priest.

name: Pontius Pilate
note: Prefect AD 26–36 (Josephus); a few scholars date his arrival to AD 19.

name: Marcellus
note: Possibly only an acting governor after Pilate's recall.

name: Tiberius Julius Alexander
note: Nephew of Philo of Alexandria.

name: Antonius Felix
note: Kept Paul in custody for two years (Acts 24:27). His recall is dated between 55 and 60; c. 58–60 is usual.

name: Porcius Festus
verses: Acts.24.27 Acts.25.1 Acts.25.4 Acts.25.9 Acts.25.12 Acts.25.13 Acts.25.14 Acts.25.22 Acts.25.23 Acts.25.24 Acts.26.24 Acts.26.25 Acts.26.32
note: Sent Paul to Rome. Arrived 59 or 60; died in office in 62.

name: Gessius Florus
note: His misrule set off the Jewish revolt (66).

name: Quirinius
note: Took the census of Judaea in AD 6 (Josephus). How this fits Luke 2:2, which sets the Nativity under Herod, is debated.

name: Gallio
note: An inscription at Delphi dates his year in Corinth to 51–52 (or 52–53), a fixed point for Paul's chronology (Acts 18:12).

name: Onias III
note: Deposed by Antiochus IV in favour of his brother Jason.

name: Jason
note: Bought the office from Antiochus IV and built a gymnasium in Jerusalem.

name: Simon ben Boethus
note: Father-in-law of Herod the Great.

name: Annas
note: Deposed in AD 15 but still called high priest in Luke 3:2 and Acts 4:6; five of his sons and his son-in-law Caiaphas held the office.

name: Caiaphas
note: Joseph Caiaphas, son-in-law of Annas; presided at the trial of Jesus. His ossuary may have been found in 1990.

name: Ananias son of Nedebeus
note: Presided when Paul was tried before the Sanhedrin (Acts 23:2).

name: Ananus ben Ananus
note: Had James the brother of Jesus stoned (AD 62); deposed after three months.

name: Phannias ben Samuel
note: The last high priest; chosen by lot by the Zealots during the revolt.
